bibliographic.title: Cosmetic Compliance and the Failure of Negotiated Governance
bibliographic.citation_apa: Krawiec, K. D. (2002). Cosmetic compliance and the failure of negotiated governance. Washington University Law Quarterly, 81, 487.

methodology.method_family: legal scholarship; doctrinal and conceptual analysis drawing on incomplete contracts literature
methodology.study_design: conceptual law review article analyzing U.S. liability regimes and governance models across multiple legal domains
methodology.sector: legal and regulatory analysis across environmental, tort, employment discrimination, corporate, securities, and health care law
methodology.technology_context: internal corporate compliance structures, legal liability mitigation, and cooperative regulation models; no AI, LLM, or conversational system technology

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The article analyzes U.S. corporate and regulatory compliance governance through legal scholarship and does not address LLMs, generative AI, conversational systems, chatbots, agents, or related technical governance mechanisms.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Although the text strongly engages governance, compliance, accountability, audit, and regulated domains such as health care and securities law, it is a 2002 legal-theoretical article on internal compliance structures and negotiated governance models. It contains no evidence on LLM-based or conversational AI systems, making it outside the technology scope of the review despite keyword overlap on governance and compliance.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Absence of LLM, generative AI, and conversational technology is explicit from title, abstract, and introduction; exclusion is unambiguous.

appraisal.notes: Appraised only on signals present in supplied excerpts. Strong conceptual clarity and legal-analytic fit within its own domain, but very low transferability to LLM conversational governance because the study is pre-AI and organization-law focused.

cerqual.explanation: The argument is internally coherent and adequately developed for legal governance scholarship, but relevance to conversational governance in LLM systems is very low because the supplied text contains no AI technology context.

coding.theme: Failure modes of cooperative regulatory governance in organizational compliance
coding.subtheme: Cosmetic compliance as legitimacy without deterrence

synthesis.main_claim: U.S. law often reduces enterprise liability for organizations with effective internal compliance structures, but growing evidence suggests such structures may not deter misconduct and may function as cosmetic window-dressing; negotiated governance models underestimate opportunistic behavior during implementation and enforcement.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a legal-theoretical critique of negotiated governance and cosmetic compliance across multiple regulated legal regimes, using incomplete contracts literature to explain governance renegotiation risks.
synthesis.limitations: Supplied excerpts do not describe empirical methods, sample, or systematic data collection; the work is conceptual legal analysis rather than an empirical or technology governance study.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from central or supporting evidence on LLM conversational governance; at most a distant analogical reference for critiques of symbolic compliance and negotiated self-governance, not for technology-specific synthesis.
